components.name: Main Magnet System
components.reasoning: This is the core component responsible for producing the strong, homogeneous magnetic field needed for MRI imaging.

components.name: Gradient Coils Assembly
components.reasoning: These coils generate short-term local variations of the main magnetic field to position and slice images in three dimensions.

components.name: RF Coil Assembly
components.reasoning: RF coils are used for both sending radiofrequency pulses into the body and receiving signals back, essential for signal generation and detection during imaging.

components.name: Patient Table
components.reasoning: Used to safely move and position patients within the MRI machine, often a separate assembly due to its size and custom fit requirements.

components.name: Control Console
components.reasoning: Houses the user interface, data acquisition systems, and computer resources for operating and interpreting images from the MRI machine.

components.name: Software Suite (Image Acquisition & Processing)
components.reasoning: Essential software that manages image capture, processing, and analysis, often provided by a specific supplier or in partnership agreements with imaging equipment manufacturers.

components.name: Cooling System
components.reasoning: Important for managing the high heat generated by various components (particularly RF coils), ensuring stable performance over long usage periods.

components.name: Shielding Panels
components.reasoning: Used to prevent external radio frequency interference and patient exposure; often fabricated separately due to its shielding properties and custom dimensions.

The use of a permanent magnet system along with gradient and RF coils are integral for generating the necessary magnetic fields required for image capture.
